big_idea: Shapes are everywhere — in art, animals, buildings. We use shapes to make pictures.
learning_intention: We are learning to use shapes and position words to make a safari picture.
student_learning_goal: I can use shapes to make a safari picture and describe it.
success_criteria: I can use 5+ shapes in my picture.
I can compose at least one bigger shape from smaller ones.
I can describe my picture using position words.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Sammy and Mira — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Safari Art Capstone Templates (1 per child)
Lesson 5 capstone rubric — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Mira: Look at this safari! A circle sun ABOVE the trees. A square hut BELOW the hill. Triangles for the giraffe!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Sammy + Mira puppets. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use everything: 2D shapes, 3D shapes, position words, compose and decompose. We make a SAFARI PICTURE.'

Review each idea quickly. 'Shapes — circle, triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon (2D). Sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid (3D). Position words — above, below, beside, inside, outside, between. Compose — put together. Decompose — break apart.'

Now show the model. Mira shows a safari picture made from shapes. Walk through:
- 'Circle SUN ABOVE the trees.'
- 'Triangle MOUNTAIN BESIDE the river.'
- 'Two triangles compose a giraffe head.'
- 'A square hut BELOW the hill.'
- 'A snake BESIDE the rock — hexagons in a row.'

'Mira says — every part of a picture is SHAPES. We use position words to say WHERE.'

Real-life: 'Look at your classroom. The clock is a circle ABOVE the door. Your desk is a rectangle BELOW your hands. Your bag is BESIDE your chair.'

Sammy's RULE: 'NAME IT — count SIDES — count CORNERS!' Today: NAME each shape, count its SIDES, count its CORNERS, name its POSITION.

Class refrain. Class chants 3x with claps: 'NAME IT — count SIDES — count CORNERS! That's how Sammy hunts!'

'Today YOU make a Safari Picture. Use 5+ shapes. Compose at least one bigger shape. Describe with position words.'

steps.instruction: Hand out capstone templates and pattern blocks. Each child plans their picture: what shapes will go where?
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Plan first. What animals? What landscape? What shapes?'

steps.instruction: Children glue or trace pattern blocks onto the template. They add details with crayons.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Compose at least 1 bigger shape from smaller ones. Use 5+ shapes total.'

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge: include a 3D model in the foreground (sphere as a planet, cube as a hut).
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Stretch: add a 3D shape to your scene.'

steps.instruction: Pair-share: each child describes their picture to a partner using shape names AND position words.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Tell your partner — what shapes and where.'

steps.instruction: Circulate to record summative evidence on the capstone rubric.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Ask 'Which shape is composed? Where is the sun?' Mark the rubric.

differentiation.for_emerging: Pre-cut shape stickers; child arranges and glues. Just identify and place.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch: include 3D models AND describe with 5+ position words AND compose 2 bigger shapes from smaller ones.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a sentence frame: 'I drew a ___ ___ the ___.' Pictures of position words on desk.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE PATH: skip the printed templates and pattern blocks. Children build the safari on the FLOOR with body shapes — pairs and trios become animals (2 children = a square hut; 3 children = a triangle mountain; 4 = a rectangular river); use position words to arrange the body-shapes spatially (body-cone ABOVE the body-cube; body-circle BESIDE the body-triangle); each child describes ONE part of the body-safari to a partner using shape names AND position words. Whole capstone runs on bodies + classroom space — no printed templates, no pattern blocks, no glue.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: uses 5+ different shapes; composes a bigger shape; describes with position words.

discussion_prompts: Show ONE shape in your picture. What is it?
Did you compose a bigger shape? Show us.
Where is the sun in your picture?
Where is the animal you drew?
consolidation.exit_routine: Refrain chant 3x. Then each child finishes the sentence: 'My favourite shape in my picture is ___ because ___' AND names the shape's position ('___ is ABOVE / BELOW / BESIDE the ___'). Sticky-note one shape and post on the Shape Safari poster.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Capstone art picture with 5+ shapes, 1+ composed shape, position-word description.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures A9.1, A9.2, A9.3, A9.4, A9.5, A9.7 in one integrated artwork.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child draws freely without using SHAPES — repairing the free-draw trap at K capstone (Clements & Sarama, 2009; Clements, Wilson & Sarama, 2004; van Hiele, 1986)
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the K shape capstone, the most-documented integrative trap is the free-draw trap: child draws curvy outlines of animals and landscape WITHOUT using shape blocks or shape names. They have all the vocabulary from D1-D4 but don't yet apply it as a SYSTEM for building pictures.

Clements, Wilson & Sarama (2004) describe the K composition trajectory: even children who can identify shapes (van Hiele Level 0/1 from D1-D2) and compose pattern-block targets (D4) may revert to free-drawing in an open-ended task because the goal frame ('this picture is MADE OF shapes') hasn't yet become automatic. The capstone is the test of whether the goal frame transfers from constrained pattern-block tasks to flexible art.

Clements & Sarama (2009) on the spatial reasoning trajectory note that K children move from Picture-maker (shapes are decoration) to Shape-composer (shapes are the SUBSTANCE of the picture) — the capstone targets this transition. Children who exit K still at Picture-maker level use shapes inconsistently in subsequent geometry work.

Van Hiele (1986) Level-1 (Analysis) — recognising shapes by their PROPERTIES — is reinforced by the capstone's verbal-description requirement (children must NAME each shape in their picture and state its POSITION). The 'identify by property' move from D1 + the position-word lattice from D3 + the compose-decompose moves from D4 ALL converge here.

Why this matters: a K child who exits the capstone with free-drawing has practiced the moves separately but hasn't INTEGRATED them. Grade 1-3 geometry assumes pictures and figures are decomposable into named shapes — the integration must land at K.

The walkthrough covers when a child draws freely.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone session. Child is drawing a curly cloud and squiggly grass. Has not used any pattern blocks. Says 'I'm drawing a safari'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch beside the child. 'Beautiful drawing! Sammy asks — can we add SHAPES too?'

Walk through. 'Look — this cloud could be a CIRCLE. This grass could have TRIANGLES for the points. This rock could be a HEXAGON.'

Give a target. 'Pick 3 shapes from the pattern blocks. Place them on your paper. Trace them. Now you have shapes IN your art.'

Generalise. 'Sammy says — pictures can be MADE OF shapes. Choose shapes, place them, trace them. That's shape art.'

If still drawing freely: hand the child shape stickers. 'Use these. Each sticker = one shape in your picture.' Force shape inclusion.

Long-term recovery: every art activity asks 'where are the shapes?'
expected_student_responses: (Strong) Composes the picture from 5+ shapes independently.
(Stretched) Composes a bigger shape from smaller ones AND uses 3D model.
common_misconceptions: Art is only free drawing. (Repair: art can be made from shapes too.)
Shapes ruin a drawing. (Repair: shapes give structure to a drawing.)
I have to use only one shape kind. (Repair: mix many shapes.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child free-draws without any shapes (Clements/Sarama Picture-maker level — shapes are decoration not substance): provide shape stickers. Each sticker = one shape in the picture. Require at least 5 stickers BEFORE any free-drawing can be added. Force the goal frame.

DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses shapes but cannot describe with property language (van Hiele Level-0 visualization, no Level-1 attribute analysis transfer from D1): pause; point at one shape they used and ask 'how many sides? How many corners?' Make them name the property AND the position. If they can't, walk back to D1 anchor chart together.

DIAGNOSTIC C — child uses shapes but doesn't compose any bigger shape from smaller ones (Picture-maker still, no D4 transfer): challenge directly: 'pick TWO triangles from your picture; what bigger shape can they MAKE together?' Trace the compose. If child can't, go back to D4's 2 triangles → square build with the pattern blocks before re-attempting the picture.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Summative artwork applying A9.1, A9.2, A9.3, A9.4, A9.5, A9.7.

Make your picture. Compose at least 1 bigger shape from smaller ones.
Describe 3 things in your picture using position words.
